newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares shake off doldrums, set record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares shake off doldrums, set record.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares powered to their eighth consecutive record close after overcoming a slightly weaker tendency in early trade.

Firming bond markets gave shares a boost, dealers said. In the current bullish environment, even laggards such as stocks of Swiss retailers saw interest, one dealer said. "It's difficult to recommend something new," he added.
Some traders thought a correction could not be ruled out in the near future.
* Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 26.4 points, or 0.61 percent, at 4,384.3 points. (revised by bourse).
The index touched an all-time high of 4,389.5 points.
* All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) climbed 12.88 points, or 0.46 percent, to 2,796.13.
Trade was heavily influenced by derivatives-linked transactions. Volume was high but was below last week's levels.

* Roche certificates were actively sought by U.S. and British investors, one dealer said. The stock jumped 245 francs to 12,435. Novartis registered shares gained nine francs to 1,702. Many investors were buying Novartis to get subscription rights for Ciba Specialty Chemicals, a Novartis subsidiary which will soon be spun off.

* Banks mostly consolidated recent gains. Credit Suisse Group lost 1.50 francs to 149.50. SBC gave up one franc to 276.50 francs. UBS bearers were off 10 francs to end at 1,239. Traders said technicals factors and insecurity stemming from the debate about possible Swiss bank accounts of Holocaust victims were behind the banks' weakness.
* Insurers Swiss Re and Baloise were in demand.
* Among industrials, ABB, Alusuisse, Holderbank and Sulzer gained ground. Alusuisse jumped 15 francs to 1,209. The company will hold its annual news conference on Tuesday.
* Trade on the Swiss Option and Futures Exchange (Soffex) turned calmer after last week's heavy volume.

The exception was call warrants in Novartis components, dealers said, noting 12,630 Sandoz calls and 3,118 Sandoz puts changed hands. Total volume in options reached 99,739 contracts with a call-put ratio of one to 1.21.
On the futures side, 3,785 SMI futures were traded, of which 3,343 were February futures.
